I am a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Physics at Auburn University. My research uses ultraviolet observations to study comets, asteroids, and interstellar objects, with a focus on cometary water activity and volatile evolution. I work often with space observatories, especially the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. I received my Ph.D. in Astronomy from the University of Hong Kong in 2023 and my B.Sc. in Astronomy from Nanjing University in 2018. I am honored to have minor planet (34712) Zexixing named after me. My home is in Bazhou city, Hebei province in Mainland China.
In addition to research, I have broad interests. I enjoy collecting from nature, photography, and sketching. The big world fascinates me.
summary: I am a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Physics at Auburn University. My research uses ultraviolet observations to study comets, asteroids, and interstellar objects, with a focus on cometary water activity and volatile evolution.
title: Zexi Xing | 邢泽曦

summary: How do comets release their ices, and what changes as they approach the Sun? I use ultraviolet observations with Swift/UVOT to trace water through OH emission, produced when sunlight breaks apart water molecules. By following water production over time and comparing it with other gases and dust, I study what drives cometary activity, how outbursts alter the coma, and how erosion exposes fresh material. These observations help connect the behavior we see today with the volatile history of a comet.
title: Cometary water and volatile evolution

summary: Interstellar comets carry material from other planetary systems into our own. My work on 2I/Borisov and 3I/ATLAS uses ultraviolet observations to measure how much water they release and how that activity changes during their passage around the Sun. Comparing water with other volatile species helps distinguish changes driven by solar heating from differences in composition. Through these rare visitors, I explore which aspects of cometary activity are shared across planetary systems and which reflect a different history.
title: Interstellar comets

summary:
Comets and asteroids move across the sky, and a comet's diffuse coma does not behave like a point source. I develop observing strategies, calibration corrections, and reduction methods that adapt Swift/UVOT to these targets, from separating faint cometary emission from background stars to extracting ultraviolet spectra blurred by motion. The aim is to turn challenging observations into reliable measurements of gas activity and asteroid reflectance.

I share these methods through [uvotimgpy](https://github.com/zexixing/uvotimgpy), a Python toolkit for small-body imaging and analysis, and [UVOTPY-for-smallbody](https://github.com/zexixing/UVOTPY-for-smallbody), extensions to UVOTPY for extracting grism spectra of moving targets and extended comae.
title: UV small-body observing toolkits
